passages.text: Now Joab son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart longed for Absalom.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the son of Zeruiah.
Joab noticed King David’s feelings.
King David’s heart longed for Absalom.
Joab understood this desire.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֖דַע יוֹאָ֣ב בֶּן־ צְרֻיָ֑ה כִּֽי־ לֵ֥ב הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עַל־ אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: So Joab sent to Tekoa to bring a wise woman from there. He told her, “Please pretend to be a mourner; put on clothes for mourning and do not anoint yourself with oil. Act like a woman who has mourned for the dead a long time.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the son of Zeruiah.
Joab sent messengers to Tekoa.
Joab brought a wise woman from Tekoa.
Joab spoke to the woman.
Joab said, “Please pretend to be a mourner.
Put on clothes for mourning.
Do not anoint yourself with oil.
Act like a woman who has mourned for the dead for many days.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יוֹאָב֙ תְּק֔וֹעָה וַיִּקַּ֥ח מִשָּׁ֖ם אִשָּׁ֣ה חֲכָמָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵ֠לֶיהָ הִֽתְאַבְּלִי־ נָ֞א וְלִבְשִׁי־ נָ֣א בִגְדֵי־ אֵ֗בֶל וְאַל־ תָּס֙וּכִי֙ שֶׁ֔מֶן וְהָיִ֕ית כְּאִשָּׁ֗ה זֶ֚ה יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים מִתְאַבֶּ֖לֶת עַל־ מֵֽת׃

passages.text: Then go to the king and speak these words to him.” And Joab put the words in her mouth.
passages.sermon:
Joab was the son of Zeruiah.
Joab sent for a wise woman from Tekoa.
Joab told the woman what to say.
Joab said, “Go to the king.”
Joab said, “Speak these words to him.”
Joab put the words in her mouth.
passages.original: וּבָאת֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְדִבַּ֥רְתְּ אֵלָ֖יו כַּדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיָּ֧שֶׂם יוֹאָ֛ב אֶת־ הַדְּבָרִ֖ים בְּפִֽיהָ׃

passages.text: When the woman from Tekoa went to the king, she fell facedown in homage and said, “Help me, O king!”
passages.sermon:
A wise woman came from Tekoa.
Joab sent her to the king.
She entered the king’s presence.
She fell facedown on the ground before him.
She bowed in respect.
She said, “Help me, O king!”
passages.original: וַ֠תֹּאמֶר הָאִשָּׁ֤ה הַתְּקֹעִית֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַתִּפֹּ֧ל עַל־ אַפֶּ֛יהָ אַ֖רְצָה וַתִּשְׁתָּ֑חוּ וַתֹּ֖אמֶר הוֹשִׁ֥עָה הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס

passages.text: “What troubles you?” the king asked her. “Indeed,” she said, “I am a widow, for my husband is dead.
passages.sermon:
The king spoke to the woman from Tekoa.
He asked her, “What troubles you?”
The woman answered the king.
She said, “I am a widow.”
She said, “My husband is dead.”
passages.original: וַיֹּֽאמֶר־ לָ֥הּ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מַה־ לָּ֑ךְ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר אֲבָ֛ל אִשָּֽׁה־ אַלְמָנָ֥ה אָ֖נִי וַיָּ֥מָת אִישִֽׁי׃

passages.text: And your maidservant had two sons who were fighting in the field with no one to separate them, and one struck the other and killed him.
passages.sermon:
The woman from Tekoa spoke to the king.
She said she was his servant.
She said she had two sons.
Her two sons fought in a field.
No one was there to separate them.
One son struck his brother.
The brother died.
passages.original: וּלְשִׁפְחָֽתְךָ֙ שְׁנֵ֣י בָנִ֔ים וַיִּנָּצ֤וּ שְׁנֵיהֶם֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה וְאֵ֥ין מַצִּ֖יל בֵּֽינֵיהֶ֑ם וַיַּכּ֧וֹ הָאֶחָ֛ד אֶת־ הָאֶחָ֖ד וַיָּ֥מֶת אֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Now the whole clan has risen up against your maidservant and said, ‘Hand over the one who struck down his brother, that we may put him to death for the life of the brother whom he killed. Then we will cut off the heir as well!’ So they would extinguish my one remaining ember by not preserving my husband’s name or posterity on the earth.”
passages.sermon:
The whole family has turned against your servant.
They said, “Give us the son who struck his brother.”
They want to put him to death for killing his brother.
They also want to destroy the heir.
If they do this, they will put out my only remaining ember.
They will not leave my husband a name or a descendant on the earth.
passages.original: וְהִנֵּה֩ קָ֨מָה כָֽל־ הַמִּשְׁפָּחָ֜ה עַל־ שִׁפְחָתֶ֗ךָ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ תְּנִ֣י׀ אֶת־ מַכֵּ֣ה אָחִ֗יו וּנְמִתֵ֙הוּ֙ בְּנֶ֤פֶשׁ אָחִיו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָרָ֔ג וְנַשְׁמִ֖ידָה גַּ֣ם אֶת־ הַיּוֹרֵ֑שׁ וְכִבּ֗וּ אֶת־ גַּֽחַלְתִּי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁאָ֔רָה לְבִלְתִּ֧י שׂוּם לְאִישִׁ֛י שֵׁ֥ם וּשְׁאֵרִ֖ית עַל־ פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃פ

passages.text: “Go home,” the king said to the woman, “and I will give orders on your behalf.”
passages.sermon:
The king spoke to the woman.
He said, "Go home."
He said, "I will give orders for you."
He promised to act on her behalf.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֶל־ הָאִשָּׁ֖ה לְכִ֣י לְבֵיתֵ֑ךְ וַאֲנִ֖י אֲצַוֶּ֥ה עָלָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: But the woman of Tekoa said to the king, “My lord the king, may any blame be on me and on my father’s house, and may the king and his throne be guiltless.”
passages.sermon:
The woman of Tekoa spoke to the king.
She said, “My lord the king, let the blame be on me.
Let the blame also be on my father’s house.
Let the king and his throne remain without guilt.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֜אמֶר הָאִשָּׁ֤ה הַתְּקוֹעִית֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עָלַ֞י אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ הֶעָוֺ֖ן וְעַל־ בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑י וְהַמֶּ֥לֶךְ וְכִסְא֖וֹ נָקִֽי׃ס

passages.text: “If anyone speaks to you,” said the king, “bring him to me, and he will not trouble you again!”
passages.sermon: The king spoke to the woman from Tekoa.\r\nHe said, “If anyone speaks to you, bring that person to me.\r\nThat person will not trouble you again.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ הַֽמְדַבֵּ֤ר אֵלַ֙יִךְ֙ וַֽהֲבֵאת֣וֹ אֵלַ֔י וְלֹֽא־ יֹסִ֥יף ע֖וֹד לָגַ֥עַת בָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: “Please,” she replied, “may the king invoke the LORD your God to prevent the avenger of blood from increasing the devastation, so that my son may not be destroyed!” “As surely as the LORD lives,” he vowed, “not a hair of your son’s head will fall to the ground.”
passages.sermon:
The woman of Tekoa spoke to King David.
She asked the king to remember the LORD his God.
She asked the king to stop the avenger of blood from destroying more.
She asked the king to protect her son from being killed.
King David answered her.
He promised by the life of the LORD.
He said that not a single hair of her son’s head would fall to the ground.
passages.original: וַתֹּאמֶר֩ יִזְכָּר־ נָ֨א הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶת־ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ מֵהַרְבִּית גֹּאֵ֤ל הַדָּם֙ לְשַׁחֵ֔ת וְלֹ֥א יַשְׁמִ֖ידוּ אֶת־ בְּנִ֑י וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ חַי־ יְהוָ֔ה אִם־ יִפֹּ֛ל מִשַּׂעֲרַ֥ת בְּנֵ֖ךְ אָֽרְצָה׃

passages.text: Then the woman said, “Please, may your servant speak a word to my lord the king?” “Speak,” he replied.
passages.sermon:
A woman spoke to the king.
She was humble and called herself his servant.
She asked the king for permission to speak.
She said, "Please, may your servant speak a word to my lord the king?"
The king answered her.
He said, "Speak."
passages.original: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה תְּדַבֶּר־ נָ֧א שִׁפְחָתְךָ֛ אֶל־ אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ דָּבָ֑ר וַיֹּ֖אמֶר דַּבֵּֽרִי׃ס

passages.text: The woman asked, “Why have you devised a thing like this against the people of God? When the king says this, does he not convict himself, since he has not brought back his own banished son?
passages.sermon:
A woman spoke to King David.
She asked him a question.
She said, “Why have you planned this against God’s people?”
She referred to the king’s actions.
She said, “When you speak this decision, you judge yourself.”
She explained her meaning.
She said, “You have not brought back your own son who is banished.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וְלָ֧מָּה חָשַׁ֛בְתָּה כָּזֹ֖את עַל־ עַ֣ם אֱלֹהִ֑ים וּמִדַּבֵּ֨ר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ הַדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ כְּאָשֵׁ֔ם לְבִלְתִּ֛י הָשִׁ֥יב הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶֽת־ נִדְּחֽוֹ׃

passages.text: For surely we will die and be like water poured out on the ground, which cannot be recovered. Yet God does not take away a life; but He devises ways that the banished one may not be cast out from Him.
passages.sermon:
All people will die.
Death is certain for everyone.
We will be like water poured out on the ground.
No one can gather water once it is spilled.
No one can bring back a life once it is gone.
God does not desire to take away life.
God thinks of ways to bring back those who are banished.
God does not want anyone to be cast away from Him.
passages.original: כִּי־ מ֣וֹת נָמ֔וּת וְכַמַּ֙יִם֙ הַנִּגָּרִ֣ים אַ֔רְצָה אֲשֶׁ֖ר לֹ֣א יֵאָסֵ֑פוּ וְלֹֽא־ יִשָּׂ֤א אֱלֹהִים֙ נֶ֔פֶשׁ וְחָשַׁב֙ מַֽחֲשָׁב֔וֹת לְבִלְתִּ֛י יִדַּ֥ח מִמֶּ֖נּוּ נִדָּֽח׃

passages.text: Now therefore, I have come to present this matter to my lord the king because the people have made me afraid. Your servant thought, ‘I will speak to the king. Perhaps he will grant the request of his maidservant.
passages.sermon:
A woman came to the king.
She wanted to speak to the king about a certain matter.
The people had made her afraid.
She was afraid because of the people.
She said to herself, “I will speak to the king.”
She hoped the king would do what she asked.
She was the king’s servant.
She hoped the king would grant her request.
passages.original: וְ֠עַתָּה אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֜אתִי לְדַבֵּ֨ר אֶל־ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ אֲדֹנִי֙ אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה כִּ֥י יֵֽרְאֻ֖נִי הָעָ֑ם וַתֹּ֤אמֶר שִׁפְחָֽתְךָ֙ אֲדַבְּרָה־ נָּ֣א אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אוּלַ֛י יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶת־ דְּבַ֥ר אֲמָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: For the king will hear and deliver his maidservant from the hand of the man who would cut off both me and my son from God’s inheritance.’
passages.sermon:
The woman spoke to King David.
She called herself his maidservant.
She said a man threatened her and her son.
This man wanted to destroy both of them.
He wanted to remove them from God’s inheritance.
She believed the king would listen to her.
She believed the king would save her from this man.
She trusted the king to deliver her and her son.
passages.original: כִּ֚י יִשְׁמַ֣ע הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶת־ אֲמָת֖וֹ מִכַּ֣ף הָאִ֑ישׁ לְהַשְׁמִ֨יד אֹתִ֤י וְאֶת־ בְּנִי֙ יַ֔חַד מִֽנַּחֲלַ֖ת אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: And now your servant says, ‘May the word of my lord the king bring me rest, for my lord the king is able to discern good and evil, just like the angel of God. May the LORD your God be with you.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The woman spoke to the king.
She was the servant of the king.
She said, “May the word of my lord the king bring me rest.”
She wanted peace and comfort from the king’s decision.
She said the king can discern good and evil.
She compared the king to the angel of God.
She said the king listens and understands both good and evil.
She prayed that the LORD, the king’s God, would be with him.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ שִׁפְחָ֣תְךָ֔ יִֽהְיֶה־ נָּ֛א דְּבַר־ אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לִמְנוּחָ֑ה כִּ֣י׀ כְּמַלְאַ֣ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים כֵּ֣ן אֲדֹנִ֤י הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ לִשְׁמֹ֙עַ֙ הַטּ֣וֹב וְהָרָ֔ע וַֽיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ יְהִ֥י עִמָּֽךְ׃פ

passages.text: Then the king said to the woman, “I am going to ask you something; do not conceal it from me!” “Let my lord the king speak,” she replied.
passages.sermon:
The king spoke to the woman.
He said, “Do not hide anything from me.
I will ask you a question.”
The woman answered the king.
She said, “Let my lord the king speak.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֣עַן הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ הָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה אַל־ נָ֨א תְכַחֲדִ֤י מִמֶּ֙נִּי֙ דָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י שֹׁאֵ֣ל אֹתָ֑ךְ וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה יְדַבֶּר־ נָ֖א אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: So the king asked, “Is the hand of Joab behind all this?” The woman answered, “As surely as you live, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right or to the left from anything that my lord the king says. Yes, your servant Joab is the one who gave me orders; he told your maidservant exactly what to say.
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to the woman.
He asked her a question.
He said, “Is Joab involved in all of this?”
The woman answered the king.
She said, “As surely as you live, my lord the king, you are always right.
No one can avoid anything you say.
Yes, your servant Joab gave me these instructions.
He told me everything I should say to you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הֲיַ֥ד יוֹאָ֛ב אִתָּ֖ךְ בְּכָל־ זֹ֑את וַתַּ֣עַן הָאִשָּׁ֣ה וַתֹּ֡אמֶר חֵֽי־ נַפְשְׁךָ֩ אֲדֹנִ֨י הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אִם־ אִ֣שׁ׀ לְהֵמִ֣ין וּלְהַשְׂמִ֗יל מִכֹּ֤ל אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבֶּר֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּֽי־ עַבְדְּךָ֤ יוֹאָב֙ ה֣וּא צִוָּ֔נִי וְה֗וּא שָׂ֚ם בְּפִ֣י שִׁפְחָֽתְךָ֔ אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

passages.text: Joab your servant has done this to bring about this change of affairs, but my lord has wisdom like the wisdom of the angel of God, to know everything that happens in the land.”
passages.sermon:
Joab is your servant.
Joab did this thing.
Joab acted to bring about this change.
My lord is wise.
My lord’s wisdom is like the wisdom of the angel of God.
My lord knows everything that happens in the land.
passages.original: לְבַעֲב֤וּר סַבֵּב֙ אֶת־ פְּנֵ֣י הַדָּבָ֔ר עָשָׂ֛ה עַבְדְּךָ֥ יוֹאָ֖ב אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַאדֹנִ֣י חָכָ֗ם כְּחָכְמַת֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים לָדַ֖עַת אֶֽת־ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּאָֽרֶץ׃ס

passages.text: Then the king said to Joab, “I hereby grant this request. Go, bring back the young man Absalom.”
passages.sermon:
The king spoke to Joab.
The king said, “I have done this thing.
Go now.
Bring back the young man Absalom.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶל־ יוֹאָ֔ב הִנֵּה־ נָ֥א עָשִׂ֖יתִי אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וְלֵ֛ךְ הָשֵׁ֥ב אֶת־ הַנַּ֖עַר אֶת־ אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Joab fell facedown in homage and blessed the king. “Today,” said Joab, “your servant knows that he has found favor with you, my lord the king, because the king has granted his request.”
passages.sermon:
Joab was the commander of King David’s army.
Joab fell facedown on the ground before the king.
Joab bowed in respect.
Joab blessed the king.
Joab said, “Today your servant knows he has found favor with you, my lord the king.
The king has granted the request of his servant.”
passages.original: וַיִּפֹּל֩ יוֹאָ֨ב אֶל־ פָּנָ֥יו אַ֛רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֶת־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֡ב הַיּוֹם֩ יָדַ֨ע עַבְדְּךָ֜ כִּי־ מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֤ן בְּעֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֥ה הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶת־ דְּבַ֥ר עַבְדּוֹ׃

passages.text: So Joab got up, went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Joab was a commander in King David’s army.
Joab stood up.
Joab traveled to Geshur.
Joab brought Absalom back from Geshur.
Joab brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
passages.original: וַיָּ֥קָם יוֹאָ֖ב וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ גְּשׁ֑וּרָה וַיָּבֵ֥א אֶת־ אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃פ

passages.text: But the king added, “He may return to his house, but he must not see my face.” So Absalom returned to his own house, but he did not see the king.
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to Absalom.
David was the king of Israel.
David said, “Absalom may return to his house.”
David also said, “Absalom must not see my face.”
Absalom went to his own house.
Absalom did not see the king.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ יִסֹּ֣ב אֶל־ בֵּית֔וֹ וּפָנַ֖י לֹ֣א יִרְאֶ֑ה וַיִּסֹּ֤ב אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֶל־ בֵּית֔וֹ וּפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֹ֥א רָאָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Now there was not a man in all Israel as handsome and highly praised as Absalom. From the sole of his foot to the top of his head, he did not have a single flaw.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was a man in Israel.
Absalom was very handsome.
No other man in Israel was as handsome as Absalom.
People praised Absalom for his appearance.
Absalom had no flaw on his body.
From the sole of his foot to the top of his head, Absalom was without defect.
passages.original: וּכְאַבְשָׁל֗וֹם לֹא־ הָיָ֧ה אִישׁ־ יָפֶ֛ה בְּכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְהַלֵּ֣ל מְאֹ֑ד מִכַּ֤ף רַגְלוֹ֙ וְעַ֣ד קָדְקֳד֔וֹ לֹא־ הָ֥יָה ב֖וֹ מֽוּם׃

passages.text: And when he cut the hair of his head—he shaved it every year because his hair got so heavy—he would weigh it out to be two hundred shekels, according to the royal standard.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was a man in Israel.
Absalom had very thick hair.
Absalom cut the hair of his head once every year.
He shaved his head because his hair became very heavy.
After he cut his hair, he weighed it.
The hair weighed two hundred shekels.
He used the royal standard to measure the weight.
passages.original: וּֽבְגַלְּחוֹ֮ אֶת־ רֹאשׁוֹ֒ וְֽ֠הָיָה מִקֵּ֨ץ יָמִ֤ים׀ לַיָּמִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְגַלֵּ֔חַ כִּֽי־ כָבֵ֥ד עָלָ֖יו וְגִלְּח֑וֹ וְשָׁקַל֙ אֶת־ שְׂעַ֣ר רֹאשׁ֔וֹ מָאתַ֥יִם שְׁקָלִ֖ים בְּאֶ֥בֶן הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: Three sons were born to Absalom, and a daughter named Tamar, who was a beautiful woman.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was a man in Israel.
Absalom had three sons.
Absalom had one daughter.
His daughter's name was Tamar.
Tamar was a beautiful woman.
passages.original: וַיִּֽוָּלְד֤וּ לְאַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ שְׁלוֹשָׁ֣ה בָנִ֔ים וּבַ֥ת אַחַ֖ת וּשְׁמָ֣הּ תָּמָ֑ר הִ֣יא הָיְתָ֔ה אִשָּׁ֖ה יְפַ֥ת מַרְאֶֽה׃פ

passages.text: Now Absalom lived in Jerusalem two years without seeing the face of the king.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom lived in Jerusalem.
He stayed there for two years.
During those two years, Absalom did not see the king.
He did not see his father, King David.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב אַבְשָׁל֛וֹם בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם שְׁנָתַ֣יִם יָמִ֑ים וּפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֹ֥א רָאָֽה׃

passages.text: Then he sent for Joab to send him to the king, but Joab refused to come to him. So Absalom sent a second time, but Joab still would not come.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom wanted to speak with King David.
Absalom sent a message to Joab.
Absalom asked Joab to go to the king for him.
Joab refused to come to Absalom.
Absalom sent for Joab a second time.
Joab still refused to come.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח אַבְשָׁל֜וֹם אֶל־ יוֹאָ֗ב לִשְׁלֹ֤חַ אֹתוֹ֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְלֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה לָב֣וֹא אֵלָ֑יו וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח עוֹד֙ שֵׁנִ֔ית וְלֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה לָבֽוֹא׃

passages.text: Then Absalom said to his servants, “Look, Joab’s field is next to mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire!” And Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom lived in Jerusalem.
Absalom could not see the king for two years.
Absalom wanted Joab to come to him, but Joab refused.
Absalom spoke to his servants.
Absalom said, "Look at Joab’s field."
Absalom said, "His field is next to mine."
Absalom said, "He has barley in his field."
Absalom said, "Go and set his field on fire."
Absalom’s servants went to Joab’s field.
Absalom’s servants set Joab’s field on fire.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֶל־ עֲבָדָ֜יו רְאוּ֩ חֶלְקַ֨ת יוֹאָ֤ב אֶל־ יָדִי֙ וְלוֹ־ שָׁ֣ם שְׂעֹרִ֔ים לְכ֖וּ וְהוֹצִתִּיהָ בָאֵ֑שׁ וַיַּצִּ֜תוּ עַבְדֵ֧י אַבְשָׁל֛וֹם אֶת־ הַחֶלְקָ֖ה בָּאֵֽשׁ׃פ

passages.text: Then Joab came to Absalom’s house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
passages.sermon:
Joab was a commander in Israel’s army.
Joab stood up.
Joab went to Absalom’s house.
Joab spoke to Absalom.
Joab asked Absalom a question.
Joab said, “Why did your servants burn my field with fire?”
passages.original: וַיָּ֣קָם יוֹאָ֔ב וַיָּבֹ֥א אֶל־ אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם הַבָּ֑יְתָה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו לָ֣מָּה הִצִּ֧יתוּ עֲבָדֶ֛ךָ אֶת־ הַחֶלְקָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר־ לִ֖י בָּאֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: “Look,” said Absalom, “I sent for you and said, ‘Come here. I want to send you to the king to ask: Why have I come back from Geshur? It would be better for me if I were still there.’ So now, let me see the king’s face, and if there is iniquity in me, let him kill me.”
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom spoke to Joab.
Absalom said, “I sent for you.
I told you, ‘Come here.’
I want to send you to the king.
I want you to ask the king a question for me.
Ask him, ‘Why have I come back from Geshur?’
It would be better for me if I were still in Geshur.
Now, let me see the king’s face.
If I am guilty of sin, let the king put me to death.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַבְשָׁל֣וֹם אֶל־ יוֹאָ֡ב הִנֵּ֣ה שָׁלַ֣חְתִּי אֵלֶ֣יךָ׀ לֵאמֹ֡ר בֹּ֣א הֵ֠נָּה וְאֶשְׁלְחָה֩ אֹתְךָ֨ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לֵאמֹ֗ר לָ֤מָּה בָּ֙אתִי֙ מִגְּשׁ֔וּר ט֥וֹב לִ֖י עֹ֣ד אֲנִי־ שָׁ֑ם וְעַתָּ֗ה אֶרְאֶה֙ פְּנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאִם־ יֶשׁ־ בִּ֥י עָוֺ֖ן וֶהֱמִתָֽנִי׃

passages.text: So Joab went and told the king, and David summoned Absalom, who came to him and bowed facedown before him. Then the king kissed Absalom.
passages.sermon:
Joab was a commander in Israel’s army.
Joab went to King David.
Joab told the king what Absalom had said.
King David called for Absalom.
Absalom came to the king.
Absalom bowed down with his face to the ground before the king.
King David kissed Absalom.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֨א יוֹאָ֣ב אֶל־ הַמֶּלֶךְ֮ וַיַּגֶּד־ לוֹ֒ וַיִּקְרָ֤א אֶל־ אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ וַיָּבֹ֣א אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיִּשְׁתַּ֨חוּ ל֧וֹ עַל־ אַפָּ֛יו אַ֖רְצָה לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיִּשַּׁ֥ק הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לְאַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃פ
